title: Customers
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers customers, suppliers and competitors together and its questions test suppliers and competitors, so it is broader than the new point's focus on customer needs and how they change, and no bank point teaches that idea at the right depth.

draft.title: Customers
card: Customers are the people or groups who buy a business's products. A new business plans what to sell, how to price it and how to promote it around what its customers need and expect.
A business can find out what customers want by asking them, for example with surveys, and by watching what they buy.
Customer needs change over time. Tastes, incomes, technology and concerns such as health can all shift what people want.
A business that keeps checking its customers can change its products as their needs change. One that does not may find its sales falling.
draft.remember: Plan around what customers want now, and keep checking as it changes.

a.q: Why does a new business ask possible customers what they want before it opens?
opts: So it can plan products and prices around their needs
So it can set its prices well above those of others
So it can avoid paying for any promotion later
So it can be sure customers will never change
a.why: Asking customers shows what they need and expect, so the business can plan what to sell and at what price. It cannot make sure customers never change, because needs shift over time.
a.clue: Think about what the answers help the owner decide.

b.q: Priya opened a bakery in Ballarat. Over two years, more customers ask for gluten-free bread, and her regular loaf sales slip. What should Priya do?
opts: Add gluten-free breads, as customer needs have changed
Keep her range the same, as her first plan was sound
Raise the price of her regular loaf to cover lost sales
Stop asking customers, as their requests are too varied
b.why: Customer needs change, and a business plans around them. Keeping the range the same ignores the shift in what customers ask for, so sales may keep falling.
b.clue: What are the customers now asking for?

a.best: So it can plan products and prices around their needs

b.best: Add gluten-free breads, as customer needs have changed
